title: Simple harmonic motion
objectives: State the defining condition for SHM, a = −ω²x, and explain each part of it.
Relate ω, period and frequency, and use T = 2π√(m/k) and T = 2π√(L/g).
Describe the phase relationships between displacement, velocity and acceleration.
Describe how kinetic and potential energy are exchanged during an oscillation.

explanation.heading: The defining condition
body: An object moves with simple harmonic motion when its acceleration is proportional to its displacement from equilibrium and directed towards equilibrium:
The minus sign is the whole point: it says the acceleration always points back towards the middle. ω is the angular frequency, in rad s⁻¹, and the period is T = 2π/ω.
A mass on a spring obeys this with ω² = k/m, so T = 2π√(m/k). A pendulum obeys it (for small angles only) with ω² = g/L, so T = 2π√(L/g).

explanation.heading: Displacement, velocity and acceleration
body: Released from rest at amplitude x₀, the motion is x = x₀ cos ωt. Differentiating gives v = −ωx₀ sin ωt and a = −ω²x₀ cos ωt.

• Speed is greatest at equilibrium: vmax = ωx₀.
  • Acceleration is greatest at the extremes: amax = ω²x₀.
  • Velocity is a quarter-cycle (π/2) out of phase with displacement; acceleration is exactly antiphase (π).
At any displacement, v = ±ω√(x₀² − x²). The period does not depend on the amplitude: a bigger swing just moves faster.

explanation.heading: Energy
body: With no friction the total energy stays constant at E = ½mω²x₀².
Energy sloshes between the two forms twice per cycle: all kinetic at equilibrium, all potential at the extremes.

demo.intro: A mass on a spring, with its displacement, velocity and acceleration plotted against time. Change the mass, spring constant and amplitude.
notice: Doubling the amplitude does not change the period, only the size of every curve.
Quadrupling the mass doubles the period, because T ∝ √m.
The acceleration curve is the displacement curve flipped upside down: a = −ω²x.

examples.title: Mass on a spring
examples.problem: A 0.50 kg mass on a spring of constant 200 N m⁻¹ oscillates with amplitude 0.040 m. Find ω, the period, the maximum speed and the maximum acceleration.
examples.answer: ω = 20 rad s⁻¹, T = 0.314 s, v_max = 0.80 m s⁻¹, a_max = 16 m s⁻²

examples.title: Speed part-way through
examples.problem: For the same oscillator, find the speed when the displacement is 0.020 m.

steps.why: Square the values carefully. Mixing cm and m here is a common slip.
Less than v_max, as expected away from equilibrium.

examples.title: Pendulum
examples.problem: Find the period of a simple pendulum of length 0.80 m.

steps.why: Valid for small angles, where sin θ ≈ θ.
Mass does not appear: every pendulum of this length has the same period.

takeaways: SHM ⇔ a = −ω²x: acceleration proportional to displacement and opposite to it.
Speed peaks at equilibrium; acceleration peaks at the extremes.
